summary.title: Frustration-driven successive metamagnetic transitions in TbB4
summary.authors: T. Inami, K. Ohwada, Y. H. Matsuda, Z. W. Ouyang, H. Nojiri, D. Okuyama, T. Matsumura, and Y. Murakami
summary.executive_summary: This study investigates the multi-step magnetization process in the Shastry-Sutherland lattice compound TbB4 using resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction (RMXD) under strong pulsed magnetic fields up to 29 T. While TbB4 possesses an XY-type ground state, which typically predicts a linear magnetization response, experiments reveal a complex multi-step metamagnetic behavior above 16 T, including a prominent one-half magnetization plateau. The authors demonstrate that these plateau phases are not purely Ising-like (collinear) but contain significant in-plane (XY) magnetic moment components, contradicting the standard expectation that plateau phases consist solely of moments aligned with the field. By analyzing the polarization dependence of the diffraction intensity, specifically the 100 reflection, the study confirms the coexistence of hard XY-type moments and Ising-like excited states. A simplified spin model incorporating both XY ground states and Ising excited states with an energy gap is proposed. Calculations using this model successfully reproduce the one-half magnetization plateau and suggest that geometric frustration inherent to the Shastry-Sutherland lattice lifts the degeneracy at critical fields, thereby driving the successive metamagnetic transitions. The work highlights that frustration can both create and break degeneracy, offering a new mechanism for understanding multi-step magnetization in frustrated magnets. The integration of high-field pulsed magnet technology with third-generation synchrotron RMXD is emphasized as a powerful tool for probing high-field magnetic structures.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study investigates the multi-step magnetization process in the Shastry-Sutherland lattice compound TbB4 using resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction (RMXD) under strong pulsed magnetic fields up to 29 T. While TbB4 possesses an XY-type ground state, which typically predicts a linear magnetization response, experiments reveal a complex multi-step metamagnetic behavior above 16 T, including a prominent one-half magnetization plateau. The authors demonstrate that these plateau phases are not purely Ising-like (collinear) but contain significant in-plane (XY) magnetic moment components, contradicting the standard expectation that plateau phases consist solely of moments aligned with the field. By analyzing the polarization dependence of the diffraction intensity, specifically the 100 reflection, the study confirms the coexistence of hard XY-type moments and Ising-like excited states. A simplified spin model incorporating both XY ground states and Ising excited states with an energy gap is proposed. Calculations using this model successfully reproduce the one-half magnetization plateau and suggest that geometric frustration inherent to the Shastry-Sutherland lattice lifts the degeneracy at critical fields, thereby driving the successive metamagnetic transitions. The work highlights that frustration can both create and break degeneracy, offering a new mechanism for understanding multi-step magnetization in frustrated magnets. The integration of high-field pulsed magnet technology with third-generation synchrotron RMXD is emphasized as a powerful tool for probing high-field magnetic structures.

Research Context
Magnetization plateaus are often ascribed to Ising spins where Sz is a good quantum number. Ising antiferromagnets like CoCl2·2H2O exhibit step-like magnetization due to finite spin combinations. Heisenberg dimers and frustrated lattices also show plateaus, but typically with collinear structures. In standard plateau phases, no ordered magnetic moment perpendicular to the field exists. TbB4 exhibits multi-step magnetization, resembling none of the previously mentioned magnet classes. TbB4 belongs to a rare class characterized by ordered perpendicular components in plateaus. Frustration plays a central role in the multi-step magnetization process of these magnets.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is how an XY-type ground state leads to multi-step metamagnetic behavior. It is hypothesized that low-lying Ising excited states exist just above the XY ground state. The origin of the multiple successive transitions is not easily understood from standard models. The study aims to determine the magnetic structure of the field-induced plateau phases. It is proposed that frustration is the key to understanding the observed multi-step magnetization. The hypothesis suggests that plateau phases contain large XY components of magnetic moments.

Methodological Details
Resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction experiments were performed on single crystals of TbB4. Experiments were conducted at the BL22XU beamline at SPring-8. The x-ray energy was tuned to the Tb LIII absorption edge at 7.514 keV. Magnetic fields up to 29 T were generated using a small pulsed magnet. The pulse duration of the magnetic field was approximately 0.6 ms. The sample was attached to a closed cycle refrigerator cold head. An avalanche photodiode was used as a high-counting-rate detector. Diffraction intensity was measured with a typical time resolution of 10 µs. The magnetic field was applied vertically and parallel to the c-axis. Sample temperature was estimated by measuring magnetic peak intensity dependence.

Procedures And Architectures
The scattering plane was horizontal with the a* axis in the plane. The 100 magnetic reflection was monitored as a function of magnetic field. Polarization dependence was analyzed to distinguish in-plane and out-of-plane moments. The scattering amplitude is proportional to m·(εi×εf). Horizontal polarization (π) incident and scattered (π') observes vertical moments. Vertical polarization (σ') senses magnetic moments in the ab-plane. A simple spin model was deduced from the experimental data. The model assumes an XY ground state and Ising excited states. Magnetization curves were calculated for finite-size cells with periodic boundary conditions. Parameters J1=2, J2=1, J3=2, and D=1 were used for calculations.

Key Results
The 100 reflection intensity remains considerable in magnetization plateau phases above 16 T. The intensity keeps a constant value between 20 and 24 T. This constant intensity corresponds to the one-half magnetization plateau. The observed intensity is about 30-50% of the intensity at 0 T. The large (1,0,0) component in plateau phases consists of ab-plane components. The calculated magnetization curve reproduces the one-half magnetization plateau. The diffraction intensity of the calculated structure is about one-quarter of the ground state. The model predicts that frustration lifts degeneracy at critical fields.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The coexistence of XY and Ising moments contradicts the expectation of collinear plateau phases. Frustration in the Shastry-Sutherland lattice lifts the degeneracy at metamagnetic transitions. This mechanism creates the observed multi-step metamagnetic behavior. Frustration acts as a general mechanism for successive metamagnetic transitions. The model captures basic features of real TbB4 despite simplifications. The scenario is common for both TbB4 and CsFeCl3.

Contradictions And Limitations
The proposed spin model is very much simplified. Interactions further than J3 must be included to account for splitting at Hc1. The model assumes no cross-term between XY and Ising spins. The experimental technique is still challenging for high-field phases. The sample surface was locally heated by synchrotron x-ray irradiation.

Claims
TbB4 plateau phases contain significant in-plane (XY) magnetic moment components. The 100 reflection intensity remains high in plateau phases. Polarization analysis confirms the ab-plane origin of the signal. Standard theory predicts collinear structures in plateaus. This indicates a mixed XY/Ising character in the plateau state.
Geometric frustration drives the successive metamagnetic transitions. Frustration lifts degeneracy at critical fields. The model reproduces the multi-step curve. Classical continuous spins on SS lattice are not strictly frustrated. Frustration can break degeneracy, not just create it.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Similar results were obtained with other parameter sets and cell sizes. 2x2 and 1x3 cells were also tested.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 2 shows the magnetic structure and magnetization process of TbB4. Figure 3 shows the energy dependence, temperature dependence, and field dependence of the 100 reflection. Figure 4 shows the calculated magnetization curve and energy diagram.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the identification of XY components in TbB4 plateau phases. 2. The strongest evidence is the polarization-dependent RMXD data confirming in-plane moments. 3. The future path is the application of RMXD to other high-field magnetic phases.
